subject.title: Context pruning mode 'off' not preventing compactions (Anthropic API key, cache-ttl smart defaults)

question: Should OpenClaw add a supported hard-limit-only or fully-off compaction mode, and should compaction entries persist a closed trigger reason for future triage?
rationale: Current source supports disabling pruning but not automatic compaction, and changing compaction safety semantics or transcript metadata is a compatibility-sensitive product decision rather than a mechanical bug fix.

options.title: Add approved hard-limit semantics
options.body: Define a supported `compaction` mode or option that preserves overflow safety while disabling threshold/safeguard compaction, with docs, tests, and upgrade behavior.

options.title: Keep safeguard-only policy
options.body: Close the disable-mode portion as unsupported and focus the remaining work only on false low-context trigger fixes and better documentation.

options.title: Defer to narrower repros
options.body: Leave this issue linked to #86684 and require live Anthropic proof before accepting any new compaction contract.

recommendation.title: Add approved hard-limit semantics
recommendation.body: Define a supported `compaction` mode or option that preserves overflow safety while disabling threshold/safeguard compaction, with docs, tests, and upgrade behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: This owner has the clearest current-history signal on the overflow/usage-accounting path that intersects the remaining low-context compaction behavior.
